title: CRIM: Composable and Reusable Item Memory for Efficient Personalized Retrieval
abstract: arXiv:2610.35323v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models incur substantial training and inference costs in personalized search and recommendation, as growing interaction histories lengthen request inputs and repeatedly expose the same item text to the model. We propose \textbf{C}omposable and \textbf{R}eusable \textbf{I}tem \textbf{M}emory (CRIM), a framework that separates item-level semantic encoding from request-level history modeling. A small set of learnable summary tokens compresses each item into compact continuous memories, while segment-level readout tokens (REC tokens) introduce predictive supervision within the interaction history. These memories are independent of users and queries and can therefore be reused across requests. At inference time, CRIM composes cached memories in interaction order and incorporates an optional query to produce a personalized retrieval representation, reducing repeated item-text encoding while retaining request-dependent contextu

translated_title: CRIM：面向高效个性化检索的可组合与可复用物品记忆
translated_abstract: 在个性化搜索与推荐任务中，大语言模型会产生高昂的训练与推理成本，原因在于不断增长的交互历史延长了请求输入，并使相同的物品文本被反复暴露给模型。我们提出了可组合与可复用物品记忆（Composable and Reusable Item Memory, CRIM），这是一个将物品级语义编码与请求级历史建模相分离的框架。一小组可学习的摘要词元将每个物品压缩为紧凑的连续记忆，同时片段级读取词元（REC词元）在交互历史内部引入预测性监督。这些记忆独立于用户和查询，因此可以在不同请求之间复用。在推理阶段，CRIM按交互顺序组合缓存的记忆，并结合可选的查询来生成个性化检索表示，在减少重复物品文本编码的同时保留与请求相关的上下文信息。
tldr: CRIM通过将物品压缩为与用户和查询无关的可复用连续记忆，并与请求级历史建模解耦，在推理时按交互顺序组合缓存记忆生成个性化检索表示，从而大幅降低大语言模型在个性化搜索与推荐中的训练与推理成本。
en_tdlr: CRIM decouples item-level semantic encoding from request-level history modeling by compressing items into user- and query-independent reusable continuous memories that are composed at inference time, significantly reducing training and inference costs for LLM-based personalized retrieval.
